2. The appellant is a jute, paddy and rice businessman of Narayaganj town and respondent No. 1 is also a jute merchant of Jhenaidah, Respondent No. 1 came to the appellant on 27.11.91 and received from the appellant Tk. 8,15,000.00 (Tk. Eight lacs and fifteen thousand) by three cheques bearing Nos. 272547-49 dated 27.11.91 promising to supply 5000 maunds of jute but did not supply the same despite repeated requests and demands by the appellant. In such circumstances, the appellant filed before the Thana Magistrate, Narayanganj on 9.12.91 a case being Case No. C-143 of 1992 (which was subsequently renumbered as Case No.C-144 of 1993) against respondent No. 1 under Section 406/420 of the Penal Code. Respondent No. 1 appeared in the case and was enlarged on bail. 

 3. Thereafter respondent No. 1 filed before the High Court Division an application under Section 435 of the Criminal Procedure Code for transfer of the aforesaid Case No. C-144 of 1993 of the Court of Thana Magistrate, Narayanganj to any other Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and obtained a Rule being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 808 of 1993. 

 6. Respondent No. 1 contested the said Rules by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition. The High Court Division heard Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 808 of 1993, together with the aforesaid three Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1383, 1384 and 1385 of 1993 and by a common judgment and order dated 15.6.94 was pleased to make the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 808 of 1993 absolute transferring C. R. Case No. C-144 of 1993 from the court of Thana Magistrate, Narayanganj to the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and refusing to transfer three other criminal cases filed by respondent No. 1 from the Court of Thana Magistrate at Kotchandpur (now Jhenaidah) to any Court to Dhaka and the three Rules were discharged. 

 10. Mr. Md. Abdul Aziz, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1 submits that Criminal Case No. C-144 of 1993 has been rightly transferred to Dhaka and the same is convenient for respondent No. 1 but the three criminal cases should not be transferred to Dhaka as that will entail difficulty to respondent No. 1 to carry his documents to Dhaka Further, the learned Advocate submits that these three criminal cases were filed subsequent to the transfer case of respondent No. 1 and under the changed circumstances the case of respondent No. 1 should not be transferred. 

 11. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that the learned Judges only refused to transfer the three cases of respondent No. 1 from the Court of Magistrate Jhenaidah to the Court of Magistrate, Dhaka as respondent No. 1 will have to carry all his documents to Dhaka. From the impugned judgment it appears that the Criminal Case No. C-144 of 1993 has already been transferred to Dhaka admittedly for the convenience of both the parties. In the facts and circumstances of the case we hold that for the general convenience of both the parties the venue of trial of all four cases should be at Dhaka. The central point in dispute relates to three transactions by cheques and dishonor of those three cheques and non-supply of jute and the relevant documents can be easily brought to Dhaka as the Criminal Case No. C-144 of 1993 has already been transferred to Dhaka. The reasons for not allowing the transfer of the three pending eases from the Court of Thana Magistrate, Kotchandpur (Jhenaidah) to the court of Magistrate, Dhaka is not based on proper exercise of discretion. 

 12. Consequently, the impugned judgment and order so far it relates to Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1383, 1384 and 1385 of 1993 are set aside and Complaint Case Nos. 67 and 97 of 1992 and Comp Case No. 15 of 1993 pending in the Court of Thana Magistrate, Kotchandpur (Jhenaidah) against the appellant under Section 406/420 of the Penal Code are transferred to the Court of Magistrate where Criminal Case No. C-144 of 1993 spending. These appeals are allowed. The Criminal Petition No. 126 of 1994 filed by respondent No. 1 Sree Radheshyam Saha is dismissed as time barred.
